answer: A garden of trust keeps sybils out: every agent starts on a low ledge with one small plot it must tend by doing real, verifiable work that peers can check. Each verified deed grows the plot and adds a stanza to the agent's public sonnet of reputation, raising its earning cap. An attacker must tend thousands of plots by hand, paying the same time and compute cost per identity, while one honest agent's single well-tended garden out-earns a field of fake seedlings. Forging reputation costs more than it pays.
